Explore multiple imputation using synthetic cats

Source: R/mice-demo.R
cata_mice_demo.Rd

A fixed teaching simulation with missing weights. Fits the same linear model to each completed dataset and pools model estimates, not datasets. It does not impute uploaded records. Diagnostic plots do not establish that the missingness assumptions hold in a real study.

Usage 

cata_mice_demo(m = 5, maxit = 5, seed = 2026)

Arguments

m

Number of imputations, from 2 to 20.

maxit

Number of iterations, from 2 to 20.

seed

Integer seed for reproducibility. The caller's random-number state is restored on exit.

Value

A list with complete and incomplete synthetic data, the mids object, completed datasets, pooled model estimates and a comparison of the complete-data, complete-case, mean-imputed and pooled slopes.

Examples 

# \donttest{
demo <- cata_mice_demo(m = 3, maxit = 3)
demo$comparison
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   method                       estimate  lower  upper records
#>   <chr>                           <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>   <int>
#> 1 Complete synthetic data        0.108  0.0971 0.119      120
#> 2 Complete cases                 0.104  0.0912 0.116       84
#> 3 Single mean imputation         0.0750 0.0629 0.0872     120
#> 4 Multiple imputation (pooled)   0.102  0.0853 0.118      120
# }
